chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) wrote to one of his companions: 'As for what follows, do not argue with the scholars, nor debate with the fools, lest the scholars hate you and the fools abuse you; and do not be lazy regarding your livelihood, lest you become a burden upon others,' or he said: 'upon your family.'
ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette regarding arguing with scholars and fools according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this epistle, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines the etiquette of social interaction, warning that engaging in futile debates with scholars leads to their alienation, while arguing with fools invites their scorn. He further links spiritual prudence to economic independence, urging the companion to avoid laziness so as not to become a burden on others or his own family, reflecting the Shia emphasis on self-sufficiency as a means of preserving dignity and facilitating worship.
